overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the November 9, 2020 meeting was accessible to the public despite two notices, and no right to public participation exists. The Clerk allegation was declined as outside the Law. The AG urged clearer notice posting.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly posted two conflicting notices for its November 9, 2020 remote meeting, with different Zoom meeting IDs, to confuse public participants.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law where its November 9 meeting was accessible to the public.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly did not allow public participation during the public hearings held as part of the November 9, 2020 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation during its meetings

allegations.summary: Complaint also alleged that the Everett City Clerk violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review any allegation that the City Clerk violated the Open Meeting Law.
